rows.public_rationale: Token-issuance endpoint by definition has no principal on entry. Content-Type dispatches to one of two grants (see primary_validator) -- neither requires a pre-existing ACR credential.

primary_validator.description: handleDeviceToken dispatches on Content-Type: 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' -> handleTokenExchange (RFC 8693 grant; subject_token = k8s SA JWT, validated via github.com/full-chaos/dev-health-go/authverify's KubernetesTokenReviewValidator -- see docs/endpoint-profiles.md '#authverify-anchor' for the full v0.5.5-pinned trace). Otherwise -> handleDeviceCodeToken (device_code poll, auth.DeviceFlow.Poll) -- which first refuses (CHAOS-6233, oauthDeviceCodeConflict) any device_code that belongs to an RFC 8628 device grant (storage.OAuthDeviceGrant present for its hash), since this legacy path mints with neither the resource nor the requested-scope subset that grant's binding requires. THIS IS THE acr_workload_identity_exchange ENDPOINT L0 left as a stated gap.

token_shape.token_type: RFC 8693 subject_token=k8s bound ServiceAccount JWT (workload grant) OR device_code (device grant)
token_shape.issuer: Kubernetes API server (validated live via TokenReview, not decoded locally -- see docs/endpoint-profiles.md)
token_shape.audience: ACR_WORKLOAD_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_AUDIENCE (workload grant only; deployment-configured, required non-empty to enable the grant at all)

rows.resource_resolver: Workload grant: {TrustDomain (static, ACR_WORKLOAD_TRUST_DOMAIN) + Namespace + ServiceAccountName + ServiceAccountUID from TokenReview} -> storage.WorkloadBindingKey lookup -> OrgID + RoleScopes(binding.Role) + RepositoryScopes. Device grant: device_code -> pre-approved org/scopes from the device_approval step.
rows.disclosure_behavior: writeTokenExchangeError()/writeOAuthDeviceError() -- ErrSubjectTokenInvalid and ErrWorkloadBindingNotFound map to the SAME invalid_grant code (device_routes.go/token_exchange_routes.go:63-68) so a disabled workload binding is indistinguishable from one that never existed.

anchor.note: device_code grant path (JSON body, handleDeviceCodeToken -> deviceFlow.Poll -> redeem): mints the fcacr_ credential on approved-device redemption

token-exchange grant path (form-urlencoded RFC 8693, handleTokenExchange -> authverify.WorkloadTokenExchangeService.Exchange -> serviceAccessTokenIssuer.Issue, wired in internal/runtime/hosted/workload_token_exchange.go:93-97): mints an fcacr_ credential tagged CredentialIssuanceProvenanceWorkloadExchange

issued_credential.issuer: acr serviceAccessTokenIssuer (via authverify.WorkloadTokenExchangeService, dev-health-go v0.5.5 -- see docs/endpoint-profiles.md 'authverify anchor')

RequireScope(credential:issue).

reachable_validators.description: Route-level check (device_routes.go:224) duplicates authenticateWebAssertion's own check (web_assertion_middleware.go:12) -- belt-and-braces, not a second DIFFERENT validator with different scope.

rows.resource_resolver: user_code + repository_scopes from body; org from the web assertion's org_id claim (bound to the approving admin's session, per web's approveDeviceAuthorization -- see web endpoint-profiles.web.json).
rows.disclosure_behavior: writeError() closed envelope.

Self-service rotation only needs a valid credential; it operates on the CALLER'S OWN principal.CredentialID, so no additional scope check is layered on.

rows.resource_resolver: principal.CredentialID (own credential only -- no id in the path/body that could target another credential).
rows.disclosure_behavior: writeSelfLifecycleError() closed shape.

rows.disclosure_behavior: writeSelfLifecycleError() closed shape.

rows.public_rationale: RFC 8414 authorization server metadata for hosted MCP clients; static configuration, no principal, no org context. Registered only when ACR_OAUTH_ISSUER/ACR_OAUTH_RESOURCES are configured.

primary_validator.description: No authenticator wrapper -- mux.HandleFunc directly; the body is built from process configuration alone.

rows.resource_resolver: None -- caller-independent static document.
rows.disclosure_behavior: Fixed RFC 8414 document (issuer, endpoints, supported methods).

rows.public_rationale: OAuth 2.1 authorization endpoint (authorization code + PKCE S256 + RFC 8707 resource) for hosted MCP clients; the caller has no credential by definition. It only starts a consent and sends the browser (302) to the web consent page with a 256-bit request handle; the handle authorizes nothing by itself -- the decision is made on POST /authorize/consent, which admits only a web assertion for the signed-in user.

primary_validator.description: OAuthService.Authorize -- verifies the client (a dynamic registration or a client ID metadata document) and the registered redirect URI before anything is redirectable (exact match, except a loopback URI registered with no port also matches any port on that same scheme/host/path/query -- RFC 8252 §7.3; localhost additionally for client ID metadata document clients only), then requires response_type=code, S256 PKCE, a configured resource and a known scope; only then starts the consent and redirects to the web consent page; rate limited per IP by AllowDeviceCreation.

rows.resource_resolver: None yet -- starts a device authorization with no hints (its raw device and user codes are discarded); org and repositories are chosen on the web consent page.
rows.disclosure_behavior: 302 to ACR_OAUTH_CONSENT_URL?handle=<handle> (no-store, Referrer-Policy no-referrer), or a 303 to the verified redirect URI with a closed OAuth error code; an unverified client/redirect gets a fixed HTML problem page (CSP default-src 'none', form-action 'none', frame-ancestors 'none') and is never redirected; error redirects go to the registered redirect URI, never the request value.

primary_validator.description: deviceApprovalHandler (the same wrapper as device_approval) requires X-ACR-Web-Assertion EXACTLY (exactly one header) and rejects if Authorization is also present, then RequireScope(credential:issue): only the web, acting for its signed-in user, can read or decide a request; the browser that holds the handle cannot.

token_shape.token_type: X-ACR-Web-Assertion (EdDSA JWT, permissions includes credential:issue, path /authorize/consent)

reachable_validators.description: OAuthService.ApproveConsent/DenyConsent/ConsentRequest -- the handle's request must be undecided and unexpired (10 minutes); approval applies the device approval's org and repository rules (ApproveForOAuth) and issues the code at most once.

rows.resource_resolver: The handle's stored authorization request; org from the web assertion's org_id claim, repositories from repository_scopes within the assertion's grant.
rows.disclosure_behavior: JSON: preview {client_name, client_self_asserted, client_kind, redirect_origin, resource, scopes, expires_at}; approve/deny {redirect_url} (the registered redirect URI with code or error=access_denied, state, iss); refusals {error} 400 invalid_request / 409 already_completed / 410 expired / 503 temporarily_unavailable; unknown and malformed handles are indistinguishable.

anchor.note: OAuthService.ApproveConsent -- approves the device authorization, then mints the one-time OAuth authorization code via s.store.IssueAuthorizationCode and returns it inside redirect_url

token_shape.token_type: OAuth authorization code (opaque, 256-bit, SHA-256 at rest, 2-minute TTL, single use) standing for an approved device authorization
token_shape.audience: the RFC 8707 resource the authorization request named (a hosted MCP endpoint URL)

reachable_validators.description: OAuthService.ExchangeDeviceCode -- the device_code grant branch (form grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code): looks up the device grant's client/resource/scope by the device code's hash, requires the same client_id, then polls the device authorization (PollDeviceGrant) for authorization_pending/slow_down/access_denied/expired_token or a token once approved. Rate limited per IP by the same AllowTokenRequest budget as the authorization_code branch.

rows.public_rationale: OAuth 2.1 token endpoint (authorization_code grant, public clients, no refresh token; CHAOS-6233 added RFC 8628's device_code grant, dispatched by the grant_type form parameter); no principal on entry by definition.

primary_validator.description: OAuthService.Exchange -- consumes the code atomically first (a refused exchange spends it), then requires the same client_id and redirect_uri, an S256 code_verifier matching the stored challenge, and a resource equal to the authorized one; redeems the approved device authorization bound to that resource. Rate limited per IP by AllowTokenRequest.

rows.resource_resolver: Authorization code -> stored request -> approved device authorization (org + repository scopes chosen at web approval).
rows.disclosure_behavior: RFC 6749 §5.2 JSON errors (invalid_grant, invalid_target, unsupported_grant_type, invalid_request); unknown, expired and used codes are indistinguishable (invalid_grant).

anchor.note: DeviceFlowService.RedeemForResource -- redeem mints the fcacr_ credential (30-day expiry) with Resource bound; the authenticator admits it only with a matching X-ACR-Resource header

rows.public_rationale: RFC 7591 dynamic client registration for public MCP clients (DCR fallback to client ID metadata documents); the caller has no credential by definition.

primary_validator.description: OAuthService.Register -- public clients only (token_endpoint_auth_method none), grant types limited to authorization_code/refresh_token/urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code (CHAOS-6233 added the device-code grant; refresh_token requests are answered without it), redirect URIs HTTPS or HTTP loopback and required only when the client wants authorization_code -- a client declaring device_code only registers with none, since the device grant has no redirect step. Rate limited per IP by AllowDeviceCreation. Registration grants nothing by itself.

rows.resource_resolver: None -- stores a public client row (client_id, name, redirect URIs).
rows.disclosure_behavior: 201 RFC 7591 client information (no secret; grant_types/response_types reflect what the stored client can actually use -- device_code always, authorization_code+code only when it has a redirect_uri) or 400 invalid_client_metadata/invalid_redirect_uri.

rows.public_rationale: RFC 8628 device authorization endpoint (CHAOS-6233): starts a device-code grant for a headless/remote MCP client with no browser or redirect of its own; the caller has no credential by definition. It reuses the same device_authorizations row and POST /api/v1/oauth/device_approval approval page an OAuth authorization-code request's browser consent already reuses internally (device_oauth.go), except the raw device_code and user_code leave the server here, as RFC 8628 requires.

primary_validator.description: OAuthService.StartDeviceAuthorization -- verifies the client (a dynamic registration or a client ID metadata document), a supported scope and a configured resource exactly like Authorize, then starts a device authorization and records the client/resource/scope /token needs when the client polls back with only the device_code; rate limited per IP by AllowDeviceCreation.

rows.resource_resolver: None yet -- issues a device_code/user_code pair bound to the client, resource and scope named in the request (storage.OAuthDeviceGrant); org and repositories are chosen at the web verification page.
rows.disclosure_behavior: 200 RFC 8628 {device_code, user_code, verification_uri, verification_uri_complete, expires_in, interval} (verification_uri_complete carries user_code as a query parameter so most users only click it) or 400 invalid_client/invalid_scope/invalid_target/invalid_request; 503 temporarily_unavailable on a dependency failure.
